blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Onboarding used to mean a folder with policies and a welcome coffee. Today, it is a full journey that starts before day one and continues for months.

A great onboarding plan has three phases. During pre-boarding, in the days before joining, the new hire receives the laptop, reads about the team and signs the contract. In the first weeks come deep introductions, shadowing, small tasks and clear goals. In the first months, there are regular check-ins with the manager and HR to make sure everything is on track.

The numbers speak for themselves. If you run a structured onboarding, new hires become productive faster and they are far less likely to leave in the first year.

items.q: According to the text, how has onboarding changed?
options: It has been reduced to a single welcome coffee
It is now a journey that begins before day one and lasts for months
It is handled entirely by the new hire
It now ends on the first day of work
items.why: "Today, it is a full journey that starts before day one and continues for months."

items.q: What happens during the pre-boarding phase?
options: The new hire receives the laptop, reads about the team and signs the contract
The new hire shadows a colleague on live tasks
items.why: "During pre-boarding… the new hire receives the laptop, reads about the team and signs the contract."

items.q: According to the text, what is the benefit of a structured onboarding?
options: Managers no longer need to run check-ins
The company can skip the contract stage
New hires become productive faster and are less likely to leave in the first year
items.why: "If you run a structured onboarding, new hires become productive faster and they are far less likely to leave in the first year."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The first weeks should include clear goals
Onboarding is worth planning across several months
The way a company welcomes people affects how long they stay
A folder of policies and a coffee are enough to welcome a new hire
items.why: Inferência: o texto contrasta o modelo antigo (pasta + café) com a jornada estruturada de hoje — o autor claramente rejeita a ideia de que aquilo baste.

items.q: The phrase "The numbers speak for themselves" suggests that…
options: the benefits are backed by measurable evidence, not just opinion
items.why: Inferência: a expressão apresenta os resultados como evidência objetiva que dispensa argumentação extra.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o novo programa de integração à equipe de RH. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making time. I want to walk you through the onboarding journey I'm proposing — six months, not six days.

The idea is simple. Every new hire gets a buddy from week one, someone outside their reporting line they can ask anything. We pair that with a light schedule of shadowing, so people learn how we actually work, not just what the handbook says. And we book the check-ins in advance — day thirty, day sixty, day ninety — so they never slip off the calendar.

Here's my concern with the way we do it now. If someone feels lost in that first week, the risk of them leaving early goes up sharply. We've seen it. So pre-boarding matters: laptop, access and a short welcome note all arrive before day one, not on it.

I know the buddy system asks something of the team. But if we invest a few hours per new hire now, we cut time to productivity later — the data we pulled points to roughly half. First impressions last, and I'd rather we owned that first week than left it to chance.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How long is the onboarding journey Emily is proposing?
items.why: "six months, not six days."

items.q: What is special about the buddy in Emily's plan?
options: They come from outside the new hire's reporting line
They are the new hire's direct manager
items.why: "a buddy from week one, someone outside their reporting line they can ask anything."

items.q: Why does Emily want the check-ins booked in advance?
options: So HR can invoice for them
So the buddy can attend them
So they never slip off the calendar
So the laptop arrives on time
items.why: "we book the check-ins in advance… so they never slip off the calendar."

items.q: What does Emily imply by "I'd rather we owned that first week than left it to chance"?
options: The first week should be actively managed rather than left unplanned
The company should skip the first week entirely
The first week is not important
New hires should organise their own first week
items.why: Inferência: "owned… than left it to chance" defende planejar deliberadamente a primeira semana em vez de deixá-la ao acaso.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's attitude toward the current process?
options: Satisfied and reluctant to change it
Critical of it, but proposing a concrete fix
items.why: Inferência: ela aponta um problema real ("my concern with the way we do it now") mas traz um plano detalhado para resolvê-lo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We start pre-boarding the moment the offer is signed." Pre-boarding is…
options: the exit interview at the end of a contract
preparing the new hire before their official first day
the final week of the probation period
items.why: Pre-boarding = pré-integração: tudo o que se faz antes do primeiro dia oficial.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "For the first month, Ana will ___ a senior analyst to see how the desk really works."
items.why: To shadow = acompanhar de perto um colega para aprender na prática.

items.q: "A good buddy system pairs each new hire with an experienced colleague." Its main purpose is to…
options: monitor the new hire's every move
give the newcomer a safe person to ask questions
items.why: Buddy system = sistema de padrinho: alguém acessível para tirar dúvidas com segurança.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Structured onboarding is proven to cut ___, so people deliver value sooner."
items.why: Time to productivity = tempo até a produtividade; reduzi-lo faz a pessoa entregar valor mais cedo.

items.q: "We plan a gentle ramp-up over the first eight weeks." A ramp-up is…
options: a gradual increase toward full workload and speed
items.why: Ramp-up = rampa de aceleração: aumento gradual até a plena capacidade.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de RH e integração. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "HR still has to sign off on the onboarding budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new buddy system team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "If we skip the 30-day check-in, small problems will pile up." To pile up means to…
items.why: Pile up = acumular-se; sem acompanhamento, os pequenos problemas se somam.

items.q: "A new hire needs time to settle in before taking on big projects." To settle in means to…
options: become comfortable in a new role or environment
items.why: Settle in = adaptar-se, sentir-se à vontade num novo ambiente.

items.q: "The manager promised weekly check-ins but never followed through." This means the manager…
options: did not carry the plan to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
